title: Jordan-Hölder Uniqueness Theorem: Composition Factors of Finite Groups in Lean

problemStatement.formal: \forall (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] (s t : CompositionSeries G), s.length = t.length \land \text{Multiset.map factors s} \cong \text{Multiset.map factors t}
problemStatement.plain: State and prove the Jordan-Hölder uniqueness theorem in Lean: the composition factors of any finite group are unique up to permutation and isomorphism. Instantiate for $S_4$ to make the $\{e\} \trianglelefteq V_4 \trianglelefteq A_4 \trianglelefteq S_4$ chain provably the unique solvability witness.
whyMatters: Foundational theorem of finite group theory, underpinning CFSG
Makes the solvability criterion for Abel-Ruffini concrete and machine-verified
Completes the bidirectional story: not just that S₄ is solvable, but that its composition factors are uniquely the abelian groups Z/2, Z/2, Z/3, Z/2

proven: Mathlib has CompositionSeries and JordanHolderModule infrastructure
Parent proof abel-ruffini-galois-extensions uses composition series implicitly
open: Explicit named Jordan-Hölder uniqueness theorem for groups (not just modules)
Concrete instantiation for S₄ with named composition factors
knownResults.goal: State jordan_holder_uniqueness as a standalone theorem and instantiate for S₄

currentState.focus: Initial problem understanding and Mathlib survey.
currentState.nextAction: Search Mathlib.GroupTheory.CompositionSeries and JordanHolder for existing uniqueness theorem.
